issues.legal_issue: An interested owner of land covered by the same acquisition notification is aggrieved when another owner obtains higher compensation for comparable land, even if the first owner received compensation without protest or did not pursue a reference.
material_facts: Owners whose land was acquired under the same notification sought redetermination after another interested owner obtained higher compensation from a civil court.
Some applicants had received the Collector’s compensation without protest or had not pursued a reference under Section 18.
issues.conclusion: An interested person who did not obtain a reference under Section 18 may seek redetermination when a civil court awards higher compensation for land covered by the same notification; receiving compensation without protest does not by itself bar that remedy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1), read with Sections 18 and 31(2), provides a separate remedy to an interested owner who failed to obtain a reference, lifting the bar that would otherwise follow from receiving compensation without protest. A higher award for comparable land under the same notification gives that owner a legal grievance. The Court applied the understanding of the remedial purpose discussed in Mewa Ram v. State of Haryana and the principle of parity for comparable land in K. Rangiah v. Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition).

rule.if: is_redetermination_application_case and interested_in_acquired_land and land_under_same_notification and did_not_obtain_section_18_reference and another_owner_received_higher_court_award_for_comparable_land

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.interested_in_acquired_land: The applicant had an interest in land that was acquired.
predicates.land_under_same_notification: The applicant’s land and the comparator land were covered by the same acquisition notification.
predicates.did_not_obtain_section_18_reference: The applicant did not obtain a court determination through a reference sought by that applicant.
predicates.another_owner_received_higher_court_awar: A court awarded another owner higher compensation for land comparable in nature, quality, situation, or value to the applicant’s land.

issues.definition: When an interested owner who did not obtain a reference owns land covered by the same notification as comparable land for which another owner obtained a higher court award, the owner may seek redetermination.

issues.legal_issue: A redetermination application must be based on an enhanced award of the court of original jurisdiction, and its time limit runs from that award rather than from a later award or appellate judgment.
material_facts: Applicants sought redetermination by relying on awards made in proceedings concerning land covered by the same acquisition notification.
The parties disputed whether later awards and appellate judgments created fresh opportunities to apply.
Section 28-A(1) allowed an application within three months of the court’s award and permitted exclusion of the day of pronouncement and the time required to obtain a copy.
issues.conclusion: The qualifying award is the award of the civil court of original jurisdiction under Section 26. The application period runs from that award, subject to the statutory exclusions; later awards and appellate judgments do not revive an expired period or create a fresh cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1) refers to an award under Part III, and Section 26(2) treats the original court’s award as a decree. An appellate decree under Section 54 or a further appeal is outside Part III and does not start a new period. The Court relied on the wording and structure of Sections 26, 28-A and 54, and held that repeated awards cannot rewrite the express limitation in Section 28-A(1).

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.enhanced_award_made_by_original_court: The court of original jurisdiction made an award granting higher compensation for the acquired land.
predicates.application_period_has_expired_from_that: The prescribed application period, after accounting for the permitted exclusions, elapsed from the original court’s award before the application was made.

issues.definition: If the application period has elapsed from the original court’s enhanced award, a later award or appellate decision does not revive the opportunity to apply.

issues.legal_issue: The redetermination remedy applies prospectively to qualifying enhanced court awards made after the provision took effect, including awards made after that point in references already pending then.
material_facts: The provision creating redetermination came into force on September 24, 1984 and was not given general retrospective effect.
Some Collector awards predated that commencement, while the references concerning them were either already decided or remained pending at commencement.
The Court distinguished references decided before commencement from pending references decided after commencement.
issues.conclusion: A court award made before commencement cannot support redetermination. If a reference was pending at commencement and the court made an enhanced award afterwards, an application may be made on that later award even if the Collector’s award predates commencement.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A is prospective because the amending legislation did not make it retrospective, unlike certain provisions for which it expressly provided retrospective or transitional operation. A later award in a reference pending at commencement uses antecedent facts but does not retrospectively reopen a concluded award. The Court applied the approach to transitional operation discussed in Union of India v. Raghubir Singh and K.S. Paripoornan v. State of Kerala.

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.qualifying_enhanced_award_made_after_rem: The original court made the enhanced award after the redetermination remedy had taken effect, including where the underlying reference was pending when the remedy took effect.

issues.definition: A person may rely on a qualifying enhanced original-court award made after the remedy took effect, subject to the other requirements for redetermination.

issues.legal_issue: A person who sought a reference and was unsuccessful cannot use the redetermination remedy to obtain the benefit of another owner’s later or more favourable award.
material_facts: Some interested persons had pursued references under Section 18 but did not succeed, or had pursued an appeal and remained unsuccessful.
Other owners obtained higher compensation in court proceedings concerning land covered by the same notification.
The statute’s redetermination remedy was framed for persons who had not made a reference application.
issues.conclusion: A person who sought and failed to obtain a reference, whether or not that person appealed, is not entitled to redetermination on the basis of another owner’s award or appellate judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1) confers its remedy on persons who had not made an application under Section 18. The non-obstante clause removes the bar for that class, but does not extend the remedy to a person who pursued and lost a reference or appeal; the final adjudication also binds the parties under res judicata principles. The Court relied on Mewa Ram v. State of Haryana and Scheduled Caste Co-operative Land Owning Society, Bhatinda v. Union of India.

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.applicant_pursued_reference: The applicant sought a court reference to challenge the compensation for the applicant’s acquired land.
predicates.applicant_was_unsuccessful: The applicant did not obtain the increased compensation sought in the reference or subsequent appeal.

issues.definition: An applicant who pursued a reference and failed cannot obtain redetermination by relying on another owner’s award.

issues.legal_issue: Limiting redetermination to interested persons who did not obtain a reference does not violate the constitutional guarantee of equality.
material_facts: The legislation extended redetermination to interested persons who had not made a reference application, but not to persons who had pursued a reference and failed.
The Court found that the legislation addressed the hardship of poor, indigent, or inarticulate owners who commonly failed to pursue references.
issues.conclusion: The distinction between persons who did not seek a reference and persons who pursued one unsuccessfully is based on an intelligible differentia related to the remedy’s purpose and does not violate Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits a classification based on an intelligible differentia that bears a reasonable relation to the object of the legislation. Section 28-A was intended to give another opportunity to persons who failed to use the reference procedure, particularly those disadvantaged by poverty or lack of knowledge; extending it to unsuccessful litigants was not constitutionally required.

predicates.is_constitutional_challenge_to_redetermi: A party challenged the constitutionality of the distinction governing who may seek redetermination.
predicates.statute_distinguishes_non_referring_owne: The legal scheme provides redetermination to owners who did not seek a reference but excludes owners who pursued one unsuccessfully.
predicates.distinction_relates_to_remedial_object: The distinction is directed to giving an additional opportunity to owners who failed to pursue the ordinary reference remedy.

issues.definition: A distinction that gives an additional opportunity to non-referring owners for the remedial purpose while excluding unsuccessful reference litigants does not violate the equality guarantee.

issues.legal_issue: A Collector must defer redetermination while an appeal concerning the court award relied on for redetermination remains pending.
material_facts: Applications for redetermination were made while appeals challenging the enhanced original-court awards were pending.
An appellate court could affirm, vary, or set aside the award on which the applications relied.
The Collector made an award in one matter before the pending appeal had been decided.
issues.conclusion: The Collector must keep timely redetermination applications pending until the appeal is finally decided, and must then determine compensation by reference to the final judgment and decree.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal is a continuation of the original proceeding, and the appellate decree is the executable decree. Deferring redetermination avoids inconsistent outcomes and unnecessary public expenditure. The Collector should obtain information or an affidavit concerning any appeal and proceed on the final appellate determination.

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.appeal_pending_against_award_relied_on: An appeal challenging the court award relied on for redetermination remained undecided when the Collector considered the application.

issues.definition: When the award supporting an application is under appeal, the Collector must wait for the final appellate decision before redetermining compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary or the State cannot seek a statutory reference against the Collector’s redetermination award, although the beneficiary may participate in the inquiry and challenge the award through constitutional review.
material_facts: A beneficiary objected to a Collector’s redetermination award and sought a reference under Section 28-A(3).
The Collector had acted as an agent for the State and beneficiary when making the compensation offer.
The beneficiary was entitled to notice and an opportunity to participate in the redetermination inquiry.
The Court noted that local legislative amendments could alter the position.
issues.conclusion: Absent an applicable local amendment conferring that right, neither the beneficiary nor the State may obtain a reference under Section 28-A(3) against the Collector’s redetermination award. A beneficiary may challenge the award under Articles 226 and 227.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 28-A(3), read with the structure of the Act, do not give the beneficiary or the State a reference right against the Collector’s award: the Collector acts on their behalf, and the statutory right to reject the offer and seek a reference belongs to the claimant. A beneficiary remains an interested person entitled to participate and may seek constitutional review where no other legal remedy exists. The Court recognized the effect of local amendments such as those in Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.

predicates.is_challenge_to_collector_redeterminatio: A party challenged a Collector’s award determining compensation after an application for redetermination.
predicates.challenger_is_beneficiary_or_state: The party seeking to challenge the award was the beneficiary of the acquisition or the State.
predicates.no_local_law_grants_reference_right: No applicable local amendment grants the beneficiary or the State a right to seek a reference against that award.

issues.definition: When the State or beneficiary challenges a redetermination award and no local law grants a reference right, it cannot obtain a statutory reference but may seek constitutional review.

issues.legal_issue: Redetermination is confined to enhanced compensation for comparable acquired land under the same notification, and does not follow from a court’s decision on an objection unrelated to compensation.
material_facts: Section 28-A applications relied on court awards concerning other land acquired under the same notification.
The statutory reference procedure allowed objections on matters including measurement, compensation, entitlement, and apportionment.
The Court held that an award resolving an objection other than the amount of compensation does not trigger redetermination.
It also held that differences in the nature, quality, or situation of land may justify a different redetermined amount.
issues.conclusion: Redetermination is available only where the court enhanced compensation for land comparable to the applicant’s land under the same notification; the same amount need not be awarded where relevant characteristics differ.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 28-A(1), 18, 21, 23 and 26 confine the remedy to enhanced compensation resulting from a reference concerning compensation. The comparator land must be sufficiently similar in relevant characteristics for its award to serve as the basis for redetermination; the Collector must consider the applicable valuation factors rather than mechanically copying the amount.

rule.if: is_redetermination_application_case and land_under_same_notification and court_enhanced_compensation_objection and comparator_land_is_comparable

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.land_under_same_notification: The applicant’s land and the comparator land were covered by the same acquisition notification.
predicates.court_enhanced_compensation_objection: The court increased compensation after deciding an objection concerning the amount of compensation.
predicates.comparator_land_is_comparable: The comparator land is comparable to the applicant’s land in relevant characteristics such as nature, quality, situation, or value.

issues.definition: A court’s enhanced compensation award may support redetermination when it concerns comparable land covered by the same notification and resolves a compensation objection.

issues.legal_issue: A timely initial redetermination application remains sufficient when the award relied on is later set aside or remitted and a fresh court award is made in the same matter.
material_facts: Applicants had already filed written applications for redetermination within the prescribed period after an original court award.
The original award was later set aside and the matter was remitted for fresh determination.
The applicants did not file new applications after the fresh determination.
issues.conclusion: A second application is not required if the initial application was already made within time; the Collector must determine the matter using the final court judgment and decree, subject to the other statutory requirements.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28-A(1) requires a timely written application. Where such an application has already been filed following the earlier award, the Court held that the requirement is satisfied despite a later remand and fresh award; the final award supplies the basis for redetermination. The Collector must still assess the application’s validity, timeliness, and the relevant compensation factors.

rule.if: is_redetermination_application_case and timely_initial_application_filed and original_award_later_set_aside_or_remitted and fresh_award_made_in_same_matter

predicates.is_redetermination_application_case: A person applied to have compensation for acquired land reconsidered on the basis of another owner’s court award.
predicates.timely_initial_application_filed: The applicant filed a written redetermination application within the prescribed period after the earlier court award.
predicates.original_award_later_set_aside_or_remitt: The court later set aside the earlier award or remitted the matter for fresh determination.
predicates.fresh_award_made_in_same_matter: A fresh court award was made in the same compensation proceeding after reconsideration.

issues.definition: A timely application filed after an earlier award need not be repeated after remand, and the final award guides the redetermination.

issues.legal_issue: The Collector should explain compensation-review rights to claimants in a language they understand and preserve a record of that explanation and of redetermination applications.
material_facts: The Court recognized that claimants may be poor, illiterate, or unaware of their rights when compensation is tendered.
It identified risks of hardship and fabricated applications after limitation periods had passed.
The Court directed safeguards concerning explanations to claimants and official registers of explanations and applications.
issues.conclusion: When tendering compensation, the Collector should explain the claimant’s rights in the claimant’s language, obtain an acknowledgment, retain a record, and maintain registers recording the relevant explanations and applications.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed administrative safeguards to reduce hardship for claimants and prevent fraudulent or antedated applications. The explanation should cover the opportunity to object to compensation and seek a reference, and should be properly recorded, particularly for an illiterate claimant.

predicates.is_compensation_tender_proceeding: A Collector was tendering compensation to a person interested in acquired land.
predicates.claimant_may_not_understand_review_right: The claimant may be unable to understand the available compensation-review procedures without an explanation in a language the claimant understands.

issues.definition: When compensation is tendered and the claimant may not understand the review procedures, the Collector should explain them in the claimant’s language and keep a record of the explanation and applications.
